name: Your project: brain health across time (example)
description:
This fictional project shows how a research team can present several related datasets through one public-facing page. The project description can explain the scientific questions, participating sites, data types, collection timeline, and governance shared across the studies.

The two example records below illustrate a structural MRI baseline dataset and a longitudinal EEG and functional MRI follow-up dataset. Each can have its own methods, participant summary, access conditions, version, and citation. These records are examples only: no participant data are hosted and no access requests or DOIs exist for them.

For a real project, this page should link to the published PN dataset versions already held in PublicnEUro. Those version-specific records remain in the full catalogue at https://datacatalog.publicneuro.eu/dataset/super/V1?tab=datasets and are the authoritative pages for discovery, access, and citation. The project page is an additional way to navigate the collection, not a replacement for individual dataset records.
